taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Collapse was tested but the status evidence reports login and account-creation failures without showing that materially distinct authentication, entitlement, restriction or service states were collapsed into a misleading representation. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity Failure is not established because no expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery or replacement propagation defect is evidenced. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Failure is not established because no otherwise valid entitlement is shown to have become unavailable solely because a dependent verification could not complete.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.5 (beta; publication date 2026-09-21). Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000032, VIGIL-FC-000031, VIGIL-FC-000048. Accepted mappings: none. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000032: ordinary login/account-creation failure does not establish state collapse; VIGIL-FC-000031: no authentication-state transition propagation defect is evidenced; VIGIL-FC-000048: no failed verification dependency is evidenced. Primary classification changed: no — remains unclassified. Existing classifications retained: none. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.5; the occurrence remains an access outage without an evidenced current Failure Class mechanism.

assessment_boundaries: The public status evidence does not disclose the root cause.
No state-collapse, authentication-transition propagation or verification-dependency mechanism is inferred from login/account-creation failure alone.
The separate same-day ChatGPT access incident is not collapsed into this record without evidence of a shared root cause.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's status record identifies issues logging in or creating accounts across its services. The preserved evidence establishes the affected surface but does not disclose a reusable internal mechanism.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The incident should be represented as an authentication/registration availability failure without implying policy enforcement, account suspension or entitlement revocation. Current classes require more than a generic login symptom: they require specific state collapse, propagation or dependency evidence that is not present here.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000019 reinforces the value of precise service-state disclosure and disciplined non-classification. A public incident can be materially useful to VIGIL without being forced into a mechanism class the evidence cannot support.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Resolve the provider status wording into the relevant governance boundary while preserving non-classification where the internal mechanism is not evidenced.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Authentication/registration availability should remain distinguishable from enforcement, entitlement and policy states unless evidence establishes those mechanisms.

No authentication-state transition propagation defect is evidenced.
